assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints as a propagation and amplification mechanism are foundational for macro-finance. The 1997 credit-cycles framework explains how small shocks become persistent downturns through asset prices and borrowing limits. It underpins the post-2008 analysis of financial crises, and it applies to both theory and policy.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore have the clearest claim through the credit-cycles model. Gertler and Gilchrist (financial accelerator, empirical work) are important but secondary. Bernanke's earlier prize covers part of the accelerator lineage, so the proposal centres on the collateral-constraint contribution.
assessment.maturity: The core paper dates from nearly 30 years ago and has been tested and extended across macro, finance and banking. It is a mature contribution with strong confirmation.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier Bernanke prize for the financial accelerator, and whether the committee would split credit between the accelerator and collateral-cycle strands.
Whether Gertler (also on B018) should be included.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the measurement of local labour-market effects of import competition changed how economists and policymakers understand inequality, automation and trade adjustment. The work is empirically credible and policy relevant, and it has produced durable methodology.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task framework and the China-shock work. Hanson is central to the trade-shock work. Katz has a long record on skill demand and inequality. Dorn and Acemoglu, who has already won, are co-contributors, so the three-name limit forces a trade-off.
assessment.maturity: The research dates from the early 2000s through the 2010s, with a large follow-on literature. Some results on persistence and magnitudes remain debated, but the main findings have broadly held up.
uncertainties: Whether Dorn deserves inclusion over Katz.
Subsequent debate on the size and persistence of the China shock and on identification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with Calvo pricing, interest-rate rules and the micro-founded policy analysis, is the workhorse of modern monetary policy. It has had very large influence on central banking practice and academic macro.
assessment.attribution: Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (policy rules and staggered contracts) and Woodford (the synthesis and normative framework) are the strongest individual claims. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler are major contributors, so credit is crowded and any trio will be contested.
assessment.maturity: The work spans four decades and has been tested in practice. It is highly mature, though the Great Inflation and ZLB experiences have prompted revisions.
uncertainties: Many strong claimants and a hard three-name cut.
Whether the committee sees the framework as sufficiently distinct from earlier macro prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law-and-finance research showed that legal origins and investor protection systematically relate to financial development and ownership structure. It opened a large comparative corporate-governance and institutions literature that is hugely cited.
assessment.attribution: The core papers were written jointly by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. The three-name limit forces dropping Vishny, whose claim is real. Shleifer also has wider contributions in behavioural finance and corporate governance.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers date from the late 1990s. The literature has been extended and also criticised, notably on legal-origin causality and measurement of the anti-director index.
uncertainties: Methodological critiques of the legal-origins identification and of index construction.
Reputational and ethical controversies around one candidate that the committee may weigh differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Household leverage and credit supply shocks were shown to drive consumption collapses and the depth of the Great Recession. The work combines granular data with macro implications and changed views of the housing-credit cycle and its policy implications.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the joint originators of the household-balance-sheet view. Campbell's contributions concern household finance and asset pricing, and the connection to this theme is less direct.
assessment.maturity: The main papers date from 2009–2014 and have been replicated and extended. The agenda is relatively recent, and some questions about external validity remain.
uncertainties: Relatively recent contribution compared with older candidates.
Ongoing debate on the credit-supply versus demand interpretation of the housing boom.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Weak-instrument diagnostics and identification-robust inference changed applied practice in IV estimation, including in labour, macro and finance. The contribution is a methodological public good with broad impact on empirical credibility.
assessment.attribution: Staiger and Stock identified and formalised the weak-instruments problem. Andrews, Moreira and Yogo built much of the robust-inference toolkit. Attribution is spread across theory and diagnostics, which makes a clean three-name selection difficult.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the 1990s through the 2010s and is well established in practice. Econometrics prizes tend to need clear, broad influence.
uncertainties: Credit split between diagnosis and the robust-testing theory.
Whether the committee judges the impact large enough for a prize relative to substantive discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data gave new measures of intergenerational mobility and of place effects, and had a strong effect on public economics and policy design. The empirical advance is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Chetty leads the agenda, with Hendren and Friedman as principal collaborators on mobility and neighbourhood effects. Katz is credited through the Moving to Opportunity work.
assessment.maturity: The main results date from 2014 onward. The agenda is productive but younger, and long-run replication and validity of some place-effect estimates are still being assessed.
uncertainties: Timing: the work may be considered early.
Debates about causal interpretation of place effects and the large team-based attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design give a general framework for how information can be strategically structured, with applications in mechanism design, regulation, markets and platforms. The theoretical contribution is clear and elegant.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow originated Bayesian persuasion. Bergemann and Morris generalised it as information design. Including Morris acknowledges the design strand but leaves out Bergemann.
assessment.maturity: The origin paper is from 2011 and the literature has grown quickly. Empirical and policy confirmation is still limited, so maturity is lower than for older candidates.
uncertainties: Limited empirical validation of the framework.
Whether the committee prefers to wait.
Credit split between the persuasion and information-design strands.
